x: In gusty conditions he finished close up to the Trinidadian Morris and American Pettigrew although no-one troubled the new Olympic Champion Quincy Watts.
Quincy Watts won the race in 44 flat - the World's leading mark for the year at that point. It was good to see Andy Lloyd in action in the UK again.

John is now rated at no. 21 of all time taking into consideration the 100/200/400. All the big names feature in the list, headed by Michael Johnson and ranging from Tommie Smith in '68 through to Quincy Watts in '92.

An enormous upset was almost caused by Du'aine Ladejo as he closed on Olympian Quincy Watts at the line, both being awarded the same time. Many felt that he had actually won. 200m: 3, J.Regis 20.31. 400m: 2, D.Ladejo 45.21. 3000mSC: 6, J.Chaston 8:29.49.
